agent_trace.summary: On abdominal CT, gallstones may be identifiable if they are calcified or have sufficient contrast with bile; however, many cholesterol stones can be difficult to see directly. The gallbladder is often assessed alongside the liver, pancreas, and biliary ducts, and CT is less sensitive for gallstones than ultrasound. The retrieved similar cases are about other abdominal CT findings, showing the expected format is a presence/absence style response based on visible anatomy.

key_facts: Gallstones are concretions within the gallbladder or biliary tree.
Calcified gallstones are more likely to be visible on CT than non-calcified cholesterol stones.
A normal gallbladder CT may show bile without visible stones.
Ultrasound is generally better than CT for detecting gallstones.
CT can also show related complications such as gallbladder wall thickening or biliary dilation.
